text: My mother had a filling done last year. It seems like the filling wasn't done properly, and the filling didn't completely remove the pulp. When she went back to the dentist, they said the tooth had become infected. They offered no …
The first time I saw a female doctor, her hands were very soft. The next time I saw a male doctor, he was a bit too heavy-handed. I couldn't sleep. I came late and took paracetamol.

Today I went to the doctor for gingivitis.
The doctor diagnosed it as tartar buildup causing swollen gums and pus. He recommended getting a tartar removal after my braces are removed and just gave me medication. That's it!!! But I went because it was swollen and painful, making it impossible to eat. I asked if the pus could be removed (my understanding, as someone who isn't a doctor, was that pus wouldn't just go away with medication; I thought it should be removed). I'd been to another clinic before where the doctor examined me, said it was due to food particles, then injected local anesthetic, drained the pus, cleaned my tooth, and gave me mouthwash and oral medication. It cleared up in 1-2 days.

After asking if the pus could be removed, the doctor here said yes. They removed the pus using a special instrument, pressing it out of the gum without any anesthetic. They pressed very hard and repeatedly; it was incredibly painful and agonizing. I cried uncontrollably on the operating table with my mouth open. It was embarrassing, but I couldn't hold back. I just burst into tears. Even without gingivitis, I would have felt pain, but this was the most excruciating pain I've ever experienced in my life – the kind of pain that makes you unable to eat.

We were told, "The dentist doesn't want to do your teeth either."
Because we said, "(Just pull the tooth out, doctor!)" because we didn't want braces. The dentist was probably unhappy and said, "Whatever, if you don't want braces, that's fine. I'm not forcing you." We were shocked that the dentist said that because we often come here with our mother and know that the dentists here are very friendly, approachable, and gentle. But after encountering this dentist, we didn't know how to act. We didn't want any problems, so we changed dentists. When we told the dentist we were changing clinics, the dentist said, "I don't want to do your teeth either." Actually, it was our fault for saying "(fuck)" to them, but we didn't expect the dentist to respond like that. We know that not all dentists are friendly, but we didn't expect this dentist to speak to us like that because the dentists we usually come to are very friendly and always give us advice. 🙏🩷
